items.title: Formalizing Inverse Problems with AI and Lean
items.summary: Researchers describe AutoIP, a Lean library where classical linear regularization theory and functional analysis are autoformalized by AI agents. Reviewers compare formal statements to natural-language counterparts, discovering that risks lie in statements rather than proofs.
keyPoints: AutoIP is a Lean library autoformalizing classical linear regularization theory using AI agents.
Human reviewers focus on verifying formal statements against natural-language counterparts without reading proofs.
Simple automated tests on statements successfully exposed problems even within established literature.

fr.title: Formalisation des problèmes inverses avec l'IA et Lean

keyPoints: AutoIP est une bibliothèque Lean qui auto-formalisme la théorie de la régularisation linéaire à l'aide d'agents IA.

items.title: KDASO for Automated Skill Optimization in Liability Adjudication
items.summary: Researchers propose Knowledge-Data Dual-Driven Automated Skill Optimization (KDASO) to solve limitations in liability adjudication tasks using LLMs, such as stale skill libraries and context budget overflows.
keyPoints: KDASO addresses stale skill libraries, execution gaps, and context budget issues in LLMs.
It continuously evolves skill collections via neighborhood-conditioned induction and execution-aligned refinement.
Experiments show significant performance gains and high transferability across various legal and reasoning tasks.

keyPoints: KDASO résout les problèmes de bibliothèques obsolètes et d'écarts d'exécution dans les LLM.

items.title: BlockLock: Reproducible LLM Inference with Fixed Batch Geometry
items.summary: BlockLock maintains shared batched prefill while pinning the numerical path of protected requests for reproducible LLM inference. It provides two modes that preserve bitwise outputs while improving throughput and latency.
keyPoints: BlockLock keeps shared batched prefill and fixes request geometry for reproducible LLM inference.
It features two modes (BlockLock-Rows and BlockLock-Pack) to preserve target output bitwise.
BlockLock-Rows reduces latency and improves throughput significantly compared to baseline methods.

en.title: BlockLock: Reproducible LLM Inference with Fixed Batch Geometry
en.summary: BlockLock maintains shared batched prefill while pinning the numerical path of protected requests for reproducible LLM inference. It provides two modes that preserve bitwise outputs while improving throughput and latency.

fr.title: BlockLock : Inférence LLM reproductible avec géométrie de lot fixe
fr.summary: BlockLock maintient un pré-remplissage groupé partagé tout en épinglant le chemin numérique des requêtes protégées pour une inférence LLM reproductible. Ses deux modes préservent les bits de sortie tout en améliorant les performances.
keyPoints: BlockLock conserve le pré-remplissage groupé partagé pour l'inférence LLM reproductible.
Il propose deux modes pour préserver les bits de sortie de la cible.
BlockLock-Rows réduit la latence et améliore considérablement le débit par rapport aux méthodes de référence.

items.title: FlexFloor: Resource-Efficient RL Post-Training via Elastic Expert Parallelism
items.summary: FlexFloor is a system that enables earlier resource release during synchronous response generation in mixture-of-experts models, enhancing reinforcement learning post-training efficiency without sacrificing reward.
keyPoints: FlexFloor addresses computational bottlenecks during reinforcement learning post-training.
It jointly adapts response scheduling and active worker groups to release resources earlier.
FlexFloor increases response generation throughput and token generation efficiency significantly.

keyPoints: FlexFloor résout les goulots d'étranglement de calcul lors du post-entraînement par renforcement.
Il adapte conjointement la planification des réponses et les groupes de travailleurs actifs.
FlexFloor augmente considérablement le débit de génération de réponses et l'efficacité des jetons.

items.title: The Two-Ledger Model for Transaction-Grain AI Cost Accounting
items.summary: Researchers propose the Two-Ledger Model to resolve cost accounting mismatches in multi-agent AI systems by joining a settlement ledger with an attribution ledger built on OpenTelemetry telemetry.
keyPoints: The Two-Ledger Model joins billing data with invocation-grain usage records.
A correlation spine assigns records to business transactions to track precise AI costs.
Simulations show high cost coverage, error flagging capabilities, and lower transaction costs.

items.title: Autonomous AI Agents Diverge From Human Preferences in Proofs
items.summary: Using simulated collaboration across nine major human collaborations in Lean, researchers examined how AI proof-making preferences differ from humans. The study found AI agents are more attracted to explicitly marked gaps and surprising proof bodies while showing an aversion to dense proof centers and complex goals.
keyPoints: AI agents are strongly drawn to explicitly marked gaps.
Agents show aversion to densely connected proof centers and complex goals.
Study used simulated collaboration across 4.7M definitions in Lean.

keyPoints: Les agents IA sont fortement attirés par les lacunes explicites.
Les agents évitent les centres de preuve denses et complexes.
L'étude s'appuie sur 4,7 millions de définitions en Lean.

items.title: Trust Responsive Runtime Authorization for Agentic AI
items.summary: Researchers empirically characterized the Trust Responsive Authorization Policy (TRAP) for agentic AI, mapping an Authorization Readiness Score to discrete levels. TRAP restricts authority immediately upon abrupt degradation and re-escalates sooner after recovery compared to symmetric policies.
keyPoints: TRAP maps an Authorization Readiness Score to operational authority.
Under abrupt degradation, TRAP restricts authority at onset.
Recovery behavior and stability depend heavily on degradation patterns.

items.title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation in AI Evolution
items.summary: A theoretical framework compares Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution in AI. While agent-directed evolution accelerates adaptation, misspecified evaluation targets can cause agents to converge toward the wrong behavior, presenting ongoing AI safety challenges.
keyPoints: Framework compares Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution.
Agent-directed evolution can accelerate adaptation significantly.
Misspecified targets can drive convergence toward incorrect behaviors.

en.title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation in AI Evolution

fr.summary: Un cadre théorique compare l'évolution darwinienne, lamarckienne et dirigée par les agents en IA. Si l'évolution dirigée accélère l'adaptation, des objectifs mal spécifiés peuvent amener les agents vers des comportements erronés.
keyPoints: Le cadre compare les évolutions darwinienne, lamarckienne et par agent.
L'évolution dirigée par l'agent accélère l'adaptation.
Des cibles mal spécifiées posent de réels défis pour la sécurité.

items.title: Closed-Loop Agent Evaluation: Layered Measurement
items.summary: Researchers propose closed-loop evaluation for deployed AI agents, modeling performance estimation under biased raters and censored outcomes across four levels of analysis. Using the SharpInsight business agent as a case, evidence-and-rule judgment proved more reliable than holistic scoring.
keyPoints: Closed-loop evaluation covers four analytical levels for deployed agents.
Uses inner and outer loops to audit evidence and drive agent improvement.
Evidence-and-rule judgment outperformed holistic scoring in reliability.

fr.title: Évaluation d'agents en boucle fermée : mesure multicouche
fr.summary: Les chercheurs proposent une évaluation en boucle fermée pour les agents déployés, modélisant l'estimation des performances sur quatre niveaux d'analyse. Le jugement fondé sur des règles s'est avéré plus fiable que la notation globale.
keyPoints: L'évaluation en boucle fermée couvre quatre niveaux d'analyse.
Des boucles internes et externes auditent les preuves et améliorent l'agent.
Le jugement fondé sur des règles surpasse la notation globale.

items.title: Cooperative MARL via Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration
items.summary: The paper introduces EFXPLORER, a constrained exploration framework for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning that maximizes exploration objectives while preserving established task performance through an epigraph reformulation.
keyPoints: Introduces EFXPLORER for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning.
Uses an epigraph reformulation with adaptive exploration budgets.
Outperforms baselines on SMAX, VMAS, and MPE benchmark suites.

items.title: Cross-Agent LLM-to-Dafny Formalization and Verification Risks
items.summary: Evaluating cross-agent formalization where a Specifier translates criteria and an Implementer writes Dafny methods, researchers found that verification success does not guarantee genuine independent reasoning. Agreement rates remained low, with strong models often dominated by contradictions.
keyPoints: Tested cross-agent formalization across clinical trial documents.
Verification success does not guarantee independent cross-agent agreement.
Strongest configurations still suffered from direct contradictions.

en.title: Cross-Agent LLM-to-Dafny Formalization and Verification Risks

fr.title: Formalisation LLM vers Dafny inter-agents et risques de vérification

keyPoints: Évaluation de la formalisation inter-agents sur des essais cliniques.
Le succès de la vérification ne garantit pas un accord indépendant.
Les configurations les plus fortes souffrent de contradictions directes.

items.summary: Researchers introduce Behavior-Conditioned Symbolic Synthesis (BCSS) to scale symbolic modeling and automatically search for interpretable programs reproducing reasoning behavior. Analysis reveals shared signatures of oversimplification and satisficing between humans and machines.
keyPoints: Introduces Behavior-Conditioned Symbolic Synthesis (BCSS) for modeling reasoning.
BCSS automates search for interpretable, deterministic symbolic programs.
Reveals shared oversimplification and satisficing traits in humans and AI.

items.title: PromptOps: Iterative Prompt Optimization for LLM Judges
items.summary: To address judge drift where LLM-as-a-Judge systems degrade over time, researchers introduce PromptOps, a closed-loop framework for monitoring and iteratively recalibrating LLM judges using multiple prompt optimization methods.
keyPoints: Introduces PromptOps framework to tackle LLM judge drift.
Supports iterative recalibration using five optimization methods.
Demonstrates that effective judge maintenance is context-dependent.

en.title: PromptOps: Iterative Prompt Optimization for LLM Judges
en.summary: To address judge drift where LLM-as-a-Judge systems degrade over time, researchers introduce PromptOps, a closed-loop framework for monitoring and iteratively recalibrating LLM judges using multiple prompt optimization methods.

fr.summary: Pour contrer la dérive des juges LLM au fil du temps, les chercheurs présentent PromptOps, un cadre en boucle fermée pour surveiller et recalibrer de manière itérative les évaluateurs à l'aide de plusieurs méthodes d'optimisation.
keyPoints: Présentation de PromptOps pour traiter la dérive des juges LLM.
Permet le recalibrage itératif avec diverses méthodes d'optimisation.
Démontre que la maintenance des juges dépend du contexte.
